intrusion.text: Teleportation made every locked door obsolete. One morning a stranger appears beside your wardrobe, holding a birthday cake and apologizing for landing in the wrong bedroom. By nightfall your city is full of people wondering who else can picture their homes.

choices.text: Use your work as an architect to make rooms difficult to picture
Help the police investigate a murder in a supposedly private house

studio.text: You design a room with crooked walls, shifting panels, and light that changes how familiar corners look. It works until a client asks you to make the place accessible to a child who is afraid of getting lost. A refuge can become another kind of trap.

choices.text: Redesign it for easy navigation, even if it is easier to picture
Keep the layout private and teach the family its landmarks

crime.text: The victim's business partner says he never entered the house. A school photo online shows the room's crooked wall, yellow chair, and blue rug. The picture might have taught the killer the way in, but a likeness is not proof of who used it.

choices.text: Preserve the image trail and demand a careful investigation
Warn every family whose home appears in public photographs

text.value: The family studies the room with you. The child remembers its landmarks better than any adult and points out a route no one had considered. The house becomes less mysterious, though the rest of the city remains open to anyone who can imagine it.
The child recognizes the room in the school photo and remembers who stood beside the camera. The clue is useful, but it does not restore the family's feeling of safety.

choices.text: Campaign for shared rules and privacy protections
Help the family build a private, confusing refuge
Refuse to let fear decide where people may go

public.text: The city adopts rules against covert scans and unauthorized entry. They cannot stop a person from arriving anywhere, but they make consent a public question rather than a private burden.

shelter.text: The family settles into its strange, carefully mapped rooms. The refuge works for them, though you know not everyone can afford to reshape a home around the world's new danger.

open_city.text: You leave the locks untouched and start a neighborhood watch built on people checking in rather than shutting one another out. It is imperfect, but the city remains more than a collection of sealed rooms.
